transport: BLE advertisement, Victron Instant Readout. Container is certainly the 0x10 Product Advertisement with the AES-CTR record described in the committed BLE PDF. THE RECORD TYPE IS NOT STATED BY ANY SOURCE FOUND for any model in this list.
sharedMapEvidence: NONE — that is the finding, and these models are grouped here only because they share the same missing evidence, not because they share a map. Every one of them is vendor-documented as having Bluetooth with Instant Readout: the BMS overview datasheet says 'All "Smart" BMS models are equipped with Bluetooth ... They all support Instant Readout'; the smallBMS NG manual rev 05 and VE.Bus BMS NG manua
gotchas: dialect: unknown. Do not write a decoder against any of these. One bench capture per model — decrypt with the device's own key and read the first byte of the record — settles each one in minutes, and that is the only thing that will.

Bluetooth on the NG BMS models can be deactivated in VictronConnect and, on the Lynx Smart BMS NG, 'can only be reactivated via a GX device'. On smallBMS NG and VE.Bus BMS NG reactivation is a power-cycle timing procedure. Losing BLE is recoverable but not obvious.
Instant Readout is disabled by default on every Victron product that has it. Bluetooth present ≠ advertising.
Per-device 16-byte AES key still required, from VictronConnect after pairing. No vendor-supported derivation.

Smart BMS CL 12/100 and Smart BMS 12/200 have Bluetooth but the BMS overview datasheet's 'Data communication' row reads 'No' for both — meaning no wired data link to a GX or an inverter/charger. BLE is the ONLY telemetry route to these two, which makes the unknown record type the whole question for them.
unmappedReports: Unknowable until the record type is known. Note that smallBMS NG — a wire-output BMS with no shunt of its own — nonetheless reports state of charge, consumed Ah and remaining time over Instant Readout, which means the NG battery packs are feeding coulomb-counted data up the M8 link. If that holds, an NG bank gives real SoC with no shunt added, which would be a genuinely useful finding once the record is identified.
